tibkafkatokof -- Apache Kafka listener/security property support in TIBCO FTL(R) Service for Kafka (FKS)

Disposition legend:
  accept         honored as written, passed through to the FKS listener
  depends        cannot be decided statically; the line states the rule
                 (e.g. a recognized class is rewritten, a custom class is flagged)
  not-applicable Kafka-internal; FTL handles it natively, so it is ignored
  unsupported    not implemented by FKS; rejected or ignored with a warning

== Listener layout ==
listeners  [accept]
    The NAME://host:port addresses the broker binds. FKS binds the client
    listeners.
advertised.listeners  [accept]
    The addresses clients are told to connect to. Passed through unchanged.
listener.security.protocol.map  [accept]
    Maps each listener name to its security protocol
    (PLAINTEXT/SSL/SASL_PLAINTEXT/SASL_SSL).
listener.name.<listener>.<property>  [accept]
    Per-listener override of any property below. Honored for the listener it
    names.
inter.broker.listener.name  [not-applicable]
    Inter-broker traffic uses the FTL servers' own connections, not a Kafka
    listener. Filtered out, not bound -- unless it is the only client-facing
    listener, in which case it is kept and bound for Kafka clients.
controller.listener.names  [not-applicable]
    The controller quorum is FTL-native (not KRaft over a Kafka listener).
    Filtered out.
control.plane.listener.name  [not-applicable]
    Control-plane traffic is carried by the FTL servers' own connections.
    Ignored.
sasl.mechanism.inter.broker.protocol  [not-applicable]
    The SASL mechanism for inter-broker traffic. Inter-broker traffic uses the
    FTL servers' own connections, not a Kafka SASL listener, so it is ignored.
sasl.mechanism.controller.protocol  [not-applicable]
    The SASL mechanism for controller traffic. The controller quorum is
    FTL-native, so it is ignored.

== TLS (server certificate and client-cert verification) ==
ssl.keystore.location  [accept]
    Path to the listener's server certificate/key used to terminate TLS on the
    Kafka listener.
ssl.keystore.password  [accept]
    Password for the server keystore. Honored.
ssl.keystore.key  [accept]
    The server private key given inline as PEM (instead of a keystore file).
    Honored.
ssl.keystore.certificate.chain  [accept]
    The server certificate chain given inline as PEM. Honored.
ssl.key.password  [accept]
    Passphrase for the server private key. Honored.
ssl.keystore.type  [depends]
    PEM is accepted directly. A Java keystore (JKS or PKCS12) is flagged
    RESOLVE-REQUIRED, because FKS reads PEM and a Java keystore would silently
    not work: convert the keystore to PEM (keytool/openssl) and set the type to
    PEM.
ssl.truststore.location  [accept]
    CA bundle used to verify inbound client certificates when the listener is
    mutual-TLS. Honored.
ssl.truststore.password  [accept]
    Password for the truststore. Honored.
ssl.truststore.certificates  [accept]
    Trusted CA certificates given inline as PEM. Honored.
ssl.truststore.type  [depends]
    Same as ssl.keystore.type: PEM is accepted; a Java truststore (JKS or
    PKCS12) is flagged RESOLVE-REQUIRED and must be converted to PEM first.
ssl.client.auth  [accept]
    none/requested/required. 'required' makes the listener mutual-TLS (the
    client certificate is verified).
ssl.enabled.protocols  [accept]
    The TLS versions the listener allows (e.g. TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3). Honored.
ssl.protocol  [accept]
    The default TLS protocol version. Honored.
ssl.cipher.suites  [accept]
    The allowed TLS cipher suites. Honored; the suite names are applied to FKS's
    OpenSSL TLS stack.
ssl.principal.mapping.rules  [depends]
    Maps a client certificate's subject DN to a principal. Simple CN extraction
    is honored; complex multi-rule sets are not fully evaluated and need review.
ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm  [not-applicable]
    Hostname verification done by a TLS client against a server's certificate.
    FKS's inbound listener verifies client certificates by CA chain, not by
    hostname, so this does not apply.
ssl.provider  [unsupported]
    Names a Java JSSE security provider. FKS uses OpenSSL, so a named Java
    provider has no effect.
ssl.secure.random.implementation  [unsupported]
    Selects a Java SecureRandom implementation. FKS uses the OpenSSL RNG; not
    applicable.
ssl.keymanager.algorithm  [unsupported]
    A Java KeyManager algorithm. FKS does not use the Java TLS stack; not
    applicable.
ssl.trustmanager.algorithm  [unsupported]
    A Java TrustManager algorithm. FKS does not use the Java TLS stack; not
    applicable.
ssl.engine.factory.class  [unsupported]
    A custom Java SSL engine. FKS terminates TLS with OpenSSL and cannot load a
    Java class.
ssl.allow.dn.changes  [not-applicable]
    Whether a certificate's DN may change across a re-authentication. FKS does
    not implement this policy.
ssl.allow.san.changes  [not-applicable]
    Whether a certificate's SANs may change across a re-authentication. FKS does
    not implement this policy.

== SASL authentication ==
sasl.enabled.mechanisms  [accept]
    The SASL mechanisms the listener offers. PLAIN and OAUTHBEARER are
    supported; SCRAM and GSSAPI are not.
sasl.jaas.config  [depends]
    Its meaning depends on the login module it names. PlainLoginModule: the
    inline user_<name>="<password>" entries are read as credentials.
    OAuthBearerLoginModule: selects OAUTHBEARER (OAuth2); the token validation
    is configured by the sasl.oauthbearer.* properties and the server callback
    handler class, not by inline users. ScramLoginModule and Kerberos
    (Krb5LoginModule) are unsupported, and any custom or delegated module is not
    run.
sasl.server.callback.handler.class  [depends]
    A Java class. A recognized standard class is translated to a FKS backend
    (e.g. oauth, inline); an unrecognized custom class cannot be run and is
    flagged RESOLVE-REQUIRED for the operator.
sasl.client.callback.handler.class  [not-applicable]
    A callback handler used by a SASL client, not by the broker accepting
    connections. Ignored.
sasl.login.callback.handler.class  [not-applicable]
    A callback handler used during a SASL client's login, not by the broker.
    Ignored.
sasl.login.class  [not-applicable]
    A custom client-side Login class. Not used by the broker's inbound listener;
    ignored.
sasl.server.max.receive.size  [not-applicable]
    Maximum size of a SASL handshake message buffer in the Java broker. FKS
    manages its own buffers.
sasl.kerberos.*  [unsupported]
    GSSAPI/Kerberos is not implemented in FKS. The whole family
    (sasl.kerberos.service.name, kinit.cmd, ticket.renew.window.factor,
    ticket.renew.jitter, min.time.before.relogin, principal.to.local.rules) is
    unsupported.
sasl.login.refresh.*  [not-applicable]
    Token-refresh timing for a SASL client maintaining its own login
    (window.factor, window.jitter, min.period.seconds, buffer.seconds). FKS's
    inbound listener validates tokens; it does not run a client login.
sasl.login.connect.timeout.ms / read.timeout.ms / retry.backoff[.max].ms  [not-applicable]
    Network tuning for a SASL client contacting a token endpoint to obtain a
    login. Not used by the broker's listener.
connections.max.reauth.ms  [accept]
    SASL re-authentication deadline (KIP-368). Honored; the connection must
    re-authenticate before it elapses.

== SASL OAUTHBEARER token validation ==
sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.url  [accept]
    The JWKS endpoint whose keys validate inbound OAUTHBEARER token signatures.
    Honored by the token validator.
sasl.oauthbearer.expected.issuer  [accept]
    The required 'iss' claim. A token whose issuer differs is rejected. Honored.
sasl.oauthbearer.expected.audience  [accept]
    The required 'aud' claim. A token whose audience does not match is rejected.
    Honored.
sasl.oauthbearer.sub.claim.name  [accept]
    Which token claim provides the principal (default 'sub'). Honored; that
    claim becomes the Kafka principal.
sasl.oauthbearer.clock.skew.seconds  [accept]
    Allowed clock skew when checking token expiry/not-before. Honored.
sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.refresh.ms  [accept]
    How often the validator refreshes the JWKS keys. Honored.
sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.retry.backoff[.max].ms  [accept]
    Retry backoff for fetching the JWKS keys. Honored.
sasl.oauthbearer.scope.claim.name  [not-applicable]
    Which claim carries OAuth scopes. FKS authorization is principal-based (ACLs
    keyed on the principal); OAuth scopes are not mapped to authorization, so
    this is ignored.
sasl.oauthbearer.token.endpoint.url  [not-applicable]
    The IdP token endpoint used to OBTAIN a token, by a producer/consumer or by
    a broker acting as an OAuth client for inter-broker auth. The FKS listener
    only validates the token a client presents (against jwks.endpoint.url); it
    never acquires one, and inter-broker auth uses the FTL servers' own
    connections, not a Kafka SASL listener. So nothing on the FKS Kafka
    listeners uses it.
sasl.oauthbearer.unsecured.*  [depends]
    Options for the unsecured (no-signature) validator used in testing. The
    OAuthBearerUnsecuredValidatorCallbackHandler is recognized as a backend, but
    an unsecured token is for testing only and must not be relied on in
    production.

== Authorization (ACLs) ==
authorizer.class.name  [depends]
    The built-in ACL authorizers are recognized:
    org.apache.kafka.metadata.authorizer.StandardAuthorizer (KRaft mode) and
    kafka.security.authorizer.AclAuthorizer (ZooKeeper mode). When one of these
    is named, the tool rewrites the value to 'KofAuthorizer' and FKS enforces
    the same ACL model: default-deny, super.users bypass, and per-principal
    allow rules. Any other authorizer is a custom Java class FKS cannot run, so
    it is flagged RESOLVE-REQUIRED.
super.users  [accept]
    Principals that bypass the ACL table. Canonicalized (User: prefix stripped)
    and installed as the bypass list.
allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found  [accept]
    When true, an operation with no matching ACL is allowed instead of denied.
    Honored; it changes the default policy.
principal.builder.class  [unsupported]
    A custom Java class that derives the principal. FKS derives the principal
    natively (cert CN / SASL username).
security.providers  [unsupported]
    Custom Java security provider classes loaded by the broker. FKS cannot load
    Java provider classes.
early.start.listeners  [not-applicable]
    Which listeners start before the KRaft metadata is caught up. The
    controller/quorum is FTL-native, so this does not apply.

== Connection limits ==
max.connections  [accept]
    Maximum concurrent connections, applied per listener. Honored; a new
    connection past the limit is refused.
max.connections.per.ip  [unsupported]
    A per-source-IP connection cap. Not implemented in this release; the setting
    is ignored.
max.connections.per.ip.overrides  [unsupported]
    Per-IP overrides of the per-IP cap. Not implemented in this release;
    ignored.
connection.failed.authentication.delay.ms  [unsupported]
    A delay before closing a connection that failed authentication. Not
    implemented; a failed auth is closed immediately.
connections.max.idle.ms  [not-applicable]
    Idle-connection timeout in the Java broker. FKS manages connection lifetime
    through the FTL servers.

== Delegation tokens ==
delegation.token.*  [unsupported]
    Delegation tokens are not implemented in FKS. The whole family
    (delegation.token.secret.key, max.lifetime.ms, expiry.time.ms,
    expiry.check.interval.ms) is unsupported.
